normalizations.reason: Each run copies the fixture into a fresh temporary folder, so its absolute path changes every run. Every spelling of that folder (as given, real path, native real path with 8.3 short and long forms on Windows, each with `/` and on Windows `\` separators and both drive-letter cases) in every encoding Go prints (raw, encoding/json escaped, and %q quoted) becomes {ROOT}; the separators and the relative path after it stay as printed. Output that already holds the literal text {ROOT}, {TIMESTAMP}, or {DATE} is escaped to {!ROOT} and so on first, so it never passes for a substituted value.

buildos-intake (front matter `timestamp`), buildos-discovery (`started_at`, `ended_at`, `qualified_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`), and buildos-design (`updated_at`) write the current UTC time in RFC 3339 form. Only time stamps inside the run window are replaced; fixture time stamps stay exact.
buildos-design names the promoted design `designs/<today>-<slug>.md` from the current date. Runs set TZ=UTC, and only `designs/<run date>-` (after `/`, `\`, or JSON-escaped `\\`) is replaced.

os_dependent_groups.summary: Prints an absolute path inside the fixture copy
os_dependent_groups.reason: The Go tools join the repository root and a relative path with path/filepath, so stdout or stderr shows `{ROOT}/...` with the operating system's separator. Go on Windows prints `\` there, and the TypeScript port prints the same spelling on each system (P1 go-path.ts). The Go output on each operating system is the parity target (PRD 20 Compatibility), so each system needs its own capture.

os_dependent_groups.summary: Prints an operating system file error
os_dependent_groups.reason: The output holds an error from a file system call (`no such file or directory`, `not a directory`) next to an absolute path inside the fixture copy. Go copies the operating system's error text, which differs on Windows (for example `The system cannot find the file specified.`), and joins the path with the system separator. The Go output on each operating system is the parity target (PRD 20 Compatibility), so each system needs its own capture.
